'''Sensitivity analysis''' studies the relation between the uncertainty in a model-based inference and the uncertainties in the model assumptions.<ref name="Risk Analysis">{{cite journal |last=Saltelli |first=A. |year=2002 |title=Sensitivity Analysis for Importance Assessment |journal=Risk Analysis |volume=22 |issue=3 |pages=1–12 |doi=10.1111/0272-4332.00040|pmid=12088235 |bibcode=2002RiskA..22..579S |citeseerx=10.1.1.194.7359 |s2cid=62191596 }}</ref><ref name="Primer">{{cite book |last1=Saltelli |first1=A. |last2=Ratto |first2=M. |last3=Andres |first3=T. |last4=Campolongo |first4=F. |last5=Cariboni |first5=J. |last6=Gatelli |first6=D. |last7=Saisana |first7=M. |last8=Tarantola |first8=S. |year=2008 |title=Global Sensitivity Analysis: The Primer |publisher=John Wiley & Sons }}</ref> Sensitivity analysis can play an important role in epidemiology, for example in assessing the influence of the unmeasured confounding on the causal conclusions of a study.<ref name="Ding">Ding, Peng; VanderWeele, Tyler J., 2016, Sensitivity Analysis Without Assumptions, Epidemiology, Volume 27 - Issue 3 - p 368-377</ref> It is also important in all mathematical modelling studies of epidemics.<ref name="CoVid19">{{cite journal |last1=Saltelli |first1=A. |last2=Bammer |first2=G. |last3=Bruno |first3=I. |last4=Charters |first4=E. |last5=Di Fiore |first5=M. |last6=Didier |first6=E. |last7=Espeland Nelson |first7=W. |last8=Kay |first8=J. |last9=Lo Piano |first9=S. |last10=Mayo |first10=D. |last11=Pielke Jr |first11=R. |last12=Portaluri |first12=T. |last13=Porter |first13=T.M. |last14=Puy |first14=A. |last15=Rafols |first15=I.|last16=Ravetz |first16=J.R. |last17=Reinert |first17=E. |last18=Sarewitz |first18=D. |last19=Stark |first19=P.B. |last20=Stirling |first20=A. |last21=van der Sluijs |first21=J. |last22=Vineis |first22=P.|year=2020 |title=Five ways to ensure that models serve society: a manifesto |journal=Nature |volume=582 |issue=7813 |pages=482–484|doi=10.1038/d41586-020-01812-9|pmid=32581374 |bibcode=2020Natur.582..482S |doi-access=free |hdl=1885/219031 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> 

Sensitivity analysis can be used in epidemiology, for example in assessing the influence of the unmeasured confounding on the causal conclusions of a study.<ref name="Ding" /><ref name="Chapter11" >Joseph AC Delaney, John D Seeger, 2013, Chapter 11, Sensitivity Analysis, in Developing a Protocol for Observational Comparative Effectiveness Research: A User's Guide, Velentgas P, Dreyer NA, Nourjah P, et al., editors, Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (US); Publication No.: 12(13)-EHC099.</ref> The use of [[sensitivity analysis]] in [[mathematical modelling of infectious disease]] is suggested in <ref name="CoVid19" /> on the [[Coronavirus disease 2019]] outbreak. Given the significant [[uncertainty]] at play, the use of [[sensitivity analysis]] to apportion the output uncertainty into input parameters is crucial in the context of [[Decision-making]]. Examples of applications of sensitivity analysis to modelling of [[COVID-19]] are <ref name="simple">{{cite journal |last1=Arino |first1=J. |last2=Portet |first2=S.| year=2020 |title=A simple model for COVID-19 |journal=Infectious Disease Modelling |volume=5 |pages=309–315|doi=10.1016/j.idm.2020.04.002|pmid=32346663 |pmc=7186130 |doi-access=free }}</ref> and.<ref name="intervention">{{cite arXiv |last1= Borgonovo|first1= E.|last2= Lu|first2= X.|eprint= 2005.01833|title= Is Time to Intervention in the COVID-19 Outbreak Really Important? A Global Sensitivity Analysis Approach|class= stat.AP|date= 2020}}</ref> in particular, the time of intervention in containing the pandemic spread is identified as a key parameter.{{cn|date=May 2023}}
